articles.title: How to use CARTMOD
articles.summary: Prepare and modify games using files you provide.
steps: Choose a task that is available in CARTMOD.
Select a cartridge or game media you have permission to use.
Review the proposed changes and any storage or save implications.
Follow the task-specific setup instructions. Importing a game does not prove it is playable.
When preparation is complete, return to Shelf to open the cartridge. Check the actual readiness status.
articles.applicability: General; individual actions depend on installed capabilities.

articles.title: Install Windows and a PC game
articles.summary: Existing DOSBox Pure guest setup procedure, subject to runtime support.
steps: Open a PC cartridge. Boot and install Windows from your own installation media.
Run the installed operating system, install the game and shut Windows down normally.
In Windows, create a Startup shortcut to the installed EXE with the game folder as Start in.
For new imports with an EXE path, copy the CARTPLAY shortcut from the content drive to Startup.
Set the installed OS as auto-start in the core menu. Shelf keeps opening the same guest when supported.
To recover setup, remove the guest startup shortcut and reopen the core menu.
articles.applicability: Transferred from PcWindowsSetupSettings.kt; verify against actual DOSBox Pure runtime before publication. Guest boot and installed-game launch are not claimed verified.

articles.title: What is emulation?
articles.summary: An emulator reproduces parts of a gaming system in software. Different titles and devices may perform differently.
articles.detail: Supported system, firmware, hardware and emulator settings can affect behaviour. Import success alone does not demonstrate compatibility.

articles.title: Does CARTDECK include games?
articles.summary: CARTDECK uses game files and media supplied by the player.
articles.detail: Only use files you are permitted to use. Game media and system firmware are not supplied by this FAQ.

articles.title: What is a game patch?
articles.summary: A patch contains changes intended for a particular version of a game.
articles.detail: The correct base file and a supported patch format are required. CARTDECK should verify the input and output before exposing a separate playable edition. Not every patch or system is supported.

articles.title: Why does an imported PC cartridge say Setup needed?
articles.summary: Creating a cartridge is different from installing and verifying its game.
articles.detail: Guest installation, boot and executable configuration may still be required. The available tasks depend on the supported runtime.

articles.title: Will a modified edition share my saves?
articles.summary: Do not assume saves are compatible between original and modified games.
articles.detail: Use the actual save scope and transfer options shown by CARTDECK. Preserve original progress and confirm any copy or replacement explicitly.

articles.title: What if setup or a patch fails?
articles.summary: Check the recorded status and error before retrying.
articles.detail: Keep your original game and saves. Use available recovery or rollback actions, and do not assume a failed preparation is ready to play.
